IAMRARE® Program Powered by NORD
Rare diseases present unique challenges for researchers and companies working towards treatments and cures:
Small patient populations;
Hard to diagnose or delayed diagnosis due to lack of education and understanding among medical professionals;
Poor understanding of the natural history of the disease and its progression without intervention;
No prior pathways to follow; clinical endpoints that are often unclear; and
Enrollment and retention challenges.
To address the special needs of those developing treatments for rare diseases, NORD has created a natural histories patient registry platform as part of the IAMRARE Program with extensive input from FDA, NIH, patients, organizations and experts in the field.
NORD’s IAMRARE Program is an easy to use system that allows patients and organizations to inform and shape medical research and translational science for rare diseases by launching high-quality, customized registries to collect the data needed to define the natural progression of their disease – ultimately advancing product development.
Learn More
Modern Powerful Features
The IAMRARE Program powerd by NORD utilizes a cutting-edge, cloud-based design that is mobile-friendly, secure and easy-to-use.
Responsive and adaptive survey design enhances the participant experience and enables natural history data tracking.
Automated survey reminders encourage long-term participant engagement.
Role-based permissions allow for flexible project management.
Data visualization tools provide participants with real-time de-identified data for comparison to other patients.
Sub-studies encourage multi stakeholder collaboration and minimize community fragmentation.
Study resources include standardized surveys and access to rare disease Institutional Review Board (IRB) expertise.

        <p><img decoding="async" class="alignnone size-full wp-image-58474" src="https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/NORD_NEWS_ClinicalCare_1024x384.jpg" alt="" width="1024" height="384" srcset="https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/NORD_NEWS_ClinicalCare_1024x384.jpg 1024w, https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/NORD_NEWS_ClinicalCare_1024x384-300x113.jpg 300w, https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/NORD_NEWS_ClinicalCare_1024x384-768x288.jpg 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></p>
<h1>IAMRARE<sup>®</sup> Program Powered by NORD</h1>
<p>Rare diseases present unique challenges for researchers and companies working towards treatments and cures:</p>
<ul>
<li>Small patient populations;</li>
<li>Hard to diagnose or delayed diagnosis due to lack of education and understanding among medical professionals;</li>
<li>Poor understanding of the natural history of the disease and its progression without intervention;</li>
<li>No prior pathways to follow; clinical endpoints that are often unclear; and</li>
<li>Enrollment and retention challenges.</li>
</ul>
<p>To address the special needs of those developing treatments for rare diseases, NORD has created a natural histories patient registry platform as part of the IAMRARE Program with extensive input from FDA, NIH, patients, organizations and experts in the field.</p>
<p>NORD’s IAMRARE Program is an easy to use system that allows patients and organizations to inform and shape medical research and translational science for rare diseases by launching high-quality, customized registries to collect the data needed to define the natural progression of their disease – ultimately advancing product development.</p>
<p><a class="button" href="https://iamrare.org/?utm_source=rarediseases_org&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=IAMRARE+Referral&utm_id=Rare+Disease+Org+Referral" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Learn More</a></p>
    </div>
</div></section><section class="fcl fcl-sb-wysiwyg theme-grey no-mt no-mr no-mb no-ml sm-pt sm-pr sm-pb sm-pl"><div class="inner">    <div class="content">
        <p><a class="alignright" style="display: block; position: relative; z-index: 2;" href="https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRD-2301-Sell-Sheet_IAMRARE-FNL.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img decoding="async" class="wp-image-271609 size-medium" src="https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRD-2301-Sell-Sheet_IAMRARE-FNL-232x300.jpg" alt="NORD Sell Sheet IAMRARE photo." width="232" height="300" srcset="https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRD-2301-Sell-Sheet_IAMRARE-FNL-232x300.jpg 232w, https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRD-2301-Sell-Sheet_IAMRARE-FNL-791x1024.jpg 791w, https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRD-2301-Sell-Sheet_IAMRARE-FNL-768x994.jpg 768w, https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRD-2301-Sell-Sheet_IAMRARE-FNL-1187x1536.jpg 1187w, https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRD-2301-Sell-Sheet_IAMRARE-FNL-1583x2048.jpg 1583w, https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRD-2301-Sell-Sheet_IAMRARE-FNL-scaled.jpg 1978w" sizes="(max-width: 232px) 100vw, 232px" /></a></p>
<h3 class="title">Modern Powerful Features</h3>
<ul>
<li>The IAMRARE Program powerd by NORD utilizes a cutting-edge, cloud-based design that is mobile-friendly, secure and easy-to-use.</li>
<li>Responsive and adaptive survey design enhances the participant experience and enables natural history data tracking.</li>
<li>Automated survey reminders encourage long-term participant engagement.</li>
<li>Role-based permissions allow for flexible project management.</li>
<li>Data visualization tools provide participants with real-time de-identified data for comparison to other patients.</li>
<li>Sub-studies encourage multi stakeholder collaboration and minimize community fragmentation.</li>
<li>Study resources include standardized surveys and access to rare disease Institutional Review Board (IRB) expertise.</li>
</ul>
<p><a class="button" href="https://rarediseases.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRD-2301-Sell-Sheet_IAMRARE-FNL.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Download One Pager</a></p>

            function parseUrlParams() {
                var params = {};
                var queryStart = url.indexOf('?') + 1;
                var queryEnd = url.indexOf('#') !== -1 ? url.indexOf('#') : url.length;
                var query = url.slice(queryStart, queryEnd);
                if (query === '') return params;
                var pairs = query.split('&');
                for (var i = 0; i < pairs.length; i++) {
                    var pair = pairs[i].split('=');
                    var key = decodeURIComponent(pair[0]);
                    var value = decodeURIComponent(pair[1] || '');

                    // Exclude pagination parameters
                    if (key.toLowerCase() === 'page' || key.toLowerCase() === 'paged' || key.toLowerCase() === 'offset') {
                        continue;
                    }
                    // If key already exists, convert to an array
                    if (params[key]) {
                        if (Array.isArray(params[key])) {
                            params[key].push(value);
                        } else {
                            params[key] = [params[key], value];
                        }
                    } else {
                        params[key] = value;
                    }
                }
                var groupedParams = {};

                Object.keys(params).forEach(function (key) {
